title: Decision of the AI Office
summary: The Decision of the AI Office sets out the rules and procedures for how artificial intelligence can be used, developed, and managed within the organization. It establishes guidelines for compliance, ethics, and decision‑making to ensure responsible AI practices.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Technology Specialists in AI
summary: The document explains how the organization will recruit and select technology specialists to fill open AI positions, outlining the skills and experience needed for these roles. It also describes the responsibilities these specialists will hold and the support structures in place to help them advance the company’s AI initiatives.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Lead Scientific Adviser
summary: The policy document announces a vacancy for the Lead Scientific Adviser position in the AI Office, outlining the responsibilities and qualifications needed for the role. It also provides details on how to apply and the selection process for interested candidates.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Legal Officers
summary: This policy outlines the process for recruiting and appointing Legal Officers to fill vacancies within the AI department. It details qualifications, responsibilities, and the steps for selection, ensuring legal compliance and expertise in AI‑related matters.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Policy Officers
summary: The policy outlines the roles and responsibilities for new AI policy officers in the office, detailing their duties in developing and overseeing AI guidelines. It also specifies the qualifications, selection criteria, and application process for filling these vacancies.

title: AI Act Scientific Panel
summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel is a group of experts convened to review and advise on the European Union’s proposed AI regulation. They evaluate scientific evidence, recommend safeguards, and help shape the law to promote safe, transparent, and accountable AI use across the EU.

title: Draft Standardisation Request
summary: The policy is a request to create new standard guidelines for AI technology. It aims to set common rules and best practices so that AI systems can be built, tested, and used consistently across different organizations.

title: CoP Consultation Notice
summary: The “CoP Consultation Notice” announces an upcoming discussion or review of the Community of Practice’s guidelines or activities. It invites stakeholders to provide input and participate in shaping future policies or procedures related to the CoP.

title: CoP Call for Expression of Interest
summary: The document announces a call for expressions of interest to establish a Community of Practice (CoP) focused on a specific AI topic. It invites stakeholders to propose and support participation in building shared knowledge and best practices.

title: CoP Graphic: Overview of Iterative Drafting Process
summary: This policy document provides a visual overview of the iterative drafting process used by a community of practice (CoP). It shows the steps of drafting, reviewing, revising, and finalizing policies through collaboration and continuous improvement.

title: CoP Graphic: Timeline of Drafting Process
summary: This policy document presents a visual timeline that shows the stages of drafting the AI policy. It highlights key milestones, dates, and the people involved in shaping the final version.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: The Code of Practice: 1st Draft outlines preliminary guidelines for how AI should be developed and used responsibly. It establishes a foundation for future policy, emphasizing ethical principles and best practices to ensure safe, trustworthy AI deployment.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: This document outlines the second draft of guidelines for professionals working with or around AI, detailing how they should conduct themselves and manage technology responsibly. It covers key areas such as risk assessment, transparency, fairness, and accountability, aiming to promote trustworthy and ethical use of AI systems.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: This document outlines the third draft of the Code of Practice, setting guidelines for responsible AI usage. It covers principles such as transparency, accountability, and user safety to ensure ethical deployment of AI systems.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft proposes a framework for responsible artificial intelligence use, outlining principles for safety, fairness, and transparency. It calls on governments, industry, and civil society to collaborate on guidelines and oversight mechanisms to ensure AI benefits society while mitigating risks.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: The AI Pact Final sets out a collective agreement on responsible AI practices, emphasizing safety, transparency, and ethical alignment. It establishes guidelines for stakeholders to collaborate on developing and deploying AI systems that benefit society while mitigating risks.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: This document outlines AI practices that are prohibited. It provides guidance to ensure AI systems comply with legal and ethical standards.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: This guide explains how to determine what counts as an AI system, outlining criteria like algorithmic decision‑making, learning components, and automated behavior. It helps organizations classify their products or services as AI so they know which rules and compliance requirements apply.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: OpenAI is outlining how clear, consistent communication can accelerate start-up growth and spur innovation across the tech ecosystem. The policy highlights key messaging strategies, stakeholder engagement practices, and resource allocation tactics to support emerging ventures and foster a thriving startup community.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups is a program that gives early‑stage companies access to powerful high‑performance computing resources and expert support. It aims to help startups grow their technology, boost innovation, and connect them with researchers and industry partners across Europe.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: The webinar covers essential ideas and strategies for managing risk. It is presented as a slideshow to guide participants through the material step by step.

title: Video: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: The webinar covers strategies for identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks related to AI deployment. It also discusses best practices for monitoring AI systems to ensure ongoing compliance and safety.
